data: Does the length of the 80% confidence interval decrease with number of samples?

The length of the 80% confidence interval decreases with the number of samples. This can be observed in all three subfigures, where the lines representing different methods generally show a downward trend as the number of samples increases. The lines for the automatic metrics (VecSim and ROUGE-1) consistently lie below the line for human evaluation, indicating lower variance and thus shorter confidence intervals. Additionally, the data efficiency (DE) values provided in the caption suggest an improvement in efficiency as the number of samples increases, which aligns with the decreasing trend of the confidence interval lengths.
